stack_slices.name: Infrastructure
stack_slices.question: Where does your product run? Cloud provider, where customer data is stored?
stack_slices.listen_for: Cloud platform, database, storage, edge hosting

stack_slices.name: Identity and access
stack_slices.question: How do your engineers log in to production? Okta, Entra, Google Workspace?
stack_slices.listen_for: Identity provider, SSO, password manager, federation

stack_slices.name: Development and deployment
stack_slices.question: How does code get from a laptop to production? Version control, CI/CD?
stack_slices.listen_for: Source control, code review, pipelines, deploys

stack_slices.name: Endpoints
stack_slices.question: What laptops do your engineers use? Any MDM or endpoint security tool?

stack_slices.name: Observability
stack_slices.question: How do you know when something breaks? Monitoring, logging, alerting, on-call?

stack_slices.name: Third-party data processors
stack_slices.question: What external services touch customer data? Payments, comms, analytics, AI, support?
stack_slices.listen_for: Payments, email/SMS, analytics, AI inference, customer support

stack_slices.name: Customer-facing
stack_slices.question: How do customers interact with your product and reach support?
stack_slices.listen_for: The product itself, status page, support tools, customer comms

stack_slices.name: Other
stack_slices.question: Backup tools, secrets managers, HR systems, internal wiki, anything I haven't asked about?
stack_slices.listen_for: Backups, secrets, HR, finance, internal docs, team chat

cloud_platform_production.reasoning_template: {name} hosts your production environment. Your service depends on their availability. We'll rely on their SOC 2 report and test how you configure their service.

managed_database.reasoning_template: {name} stores your customer data. We'll rely on their SOC 2 for storage and encryption controls, and test how you configure access and retention.

ai_inference.reasoning_template: {name} processes inference requests (which often contain customer data). We'll rely on their SOC 2 or equivalent attestation, and review your DPA.

payment_processor.reasoning_template: {name} handles payment data on your behalf. We'll rely on their SOC 2 and PCI-DSS attestation.

email_service.reasoning_template: {name} delivers your transactional email. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

sms_voice.reasoning_template: {name} delivers SMS or voice for your product. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

analytics.reasoning_template: {name} processes user analytics. We'll rely on their SOC 2 and verify your DPA covers their use.

customer_support_tool.reasoning_template: {name} stores customer conversations. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

dns.reasoning_template: {name} routes traffic to your service. We'll rely on their uptime guarantees and SOC 2 / ISO.

cdn_waf.reasoning_template: {name} sits in front of your application. We'll rely on their SOC 2 for the platform, and test how you configure WAF rules.

identity_provider.reasoning_template: {name} is where you control who can access your systems. We'll test how you configure access policies, MFA, and provisioning.

code_repository.reasoning_template: {name} holds your code and gates production deploys. We'll test branch protection, code review, secret scanning.

ci_cd_pipeline.reasoning_template: {name} ships code to production. We'll test how changes flow through it and how secrets are protected.

monitoring_logging.reasoning_template: {name} watches your production environment. We'll test how alerts route and how long logs are retained.

oncall_alerting.reasoning_template: {name} pages your on-call. We'll test alert routing and rotation.

endpoint_mdm.reasoning_template: {name} manages your workforce laptops. We'll test device compliance for anyone with production access.

endpoint_edr.reasoning_template: {name} protects your workforce devices. We'll test deployment coverage and alert handling.

secrets_manager_workforce.reasoning_template: {name} stores workforce credentials. We'll test access policies and admin controls.

secrets_manager_infra.reasoning_template: {name} stores infrastructure credentials. We'll test rotation, access policies, and auditability.

backup_service.reasoning_template: {name} backs up your customer data. We'll test backup completeness, retention, and restore testing.

hr_system.reasoning_template: {name} drives employee onboarding and offboarding. We'll test how access provisioning ties to it.

vulnerability_scanner.reasoning_template: {name} finds vulnerabilities. We'll test scan coverage and remediation tracking.

project_management.reasoning_template: {name} is internal team coordination. Not in audit scope unless you store customer data here.

internal_wiki.reasoning_template: {name} is internal documentation. We may pull policy docs as evidence, but the tool itself isn't audited. Note: becomes in scope if you store customer data here.

team_chat.reasoning_template: {name} is internal communication. We may pull incident response or change records as evidence. The tool itself isn't audited.

finance_accounting.reasoning_template: {name} is financial accounting. Not in SOC 2 scope unless it touches customer data.

office_productivity.reasoning_template: {name} is a productivity bundle (email, docs, file storage). Not in SOC 2 scope on its own. The in-scope pieces (Entra ID for production SSO, Intune for MDM, SharePoint if customer data lives there) are classified separately as their own systems. If the client confirms one of those is used for production, add it as a separate system.

subprocessor_data_warehouse.reasoning_template: {name} stores your data warehouse including customer data. We'll rely on their SOC 2 and test how you configure access.

gpu_compute.reasoning_template: {name} runs your AI workloads on managed GPU infrastructure. Customer inputs hit their machines. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

vector_database.reasoning_template: {name} stores your embeddings, which often encode customer data. We'll rely on their SOC 2 and test how you configure access.

llm_observability.reasoning_template: {name} ingests your LLM prompt and response traces, which routinely contain customer data. We'll rely on their SOC 2 and review your DPA.

ai_eval_platform.reasoning_template: {name} runs evaluations on your model outputs, often against production data. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

realtime_data_layer.reasoning_template: {name} is part of your live data path. Customer data flows through it. We'll rely on their SOC 2.

booking_scheduling.reasoning_template: {name} schedules meetings. Usually not in scope unless it stores customer-identifying info you committed to protect.

crm.reasoning_template: {name} is a sales/CRM tool holding prospect and business-contact data, not your product's customer data. Out of SOC 2 scope on its own. If product or support data syncs into {name} (in-app events, support history, customer records), tell us, since that changes its role.

builder_tool.reasoning_template: {name} is an AI coding/builder tool your team develops with. Not a SOC 2 system on its own. How code reaches production (repository, review, CI/CD) is covered under change management. Reclassify if engineers run it against customer data or production assets live in it.

corporate_email.reasoning_template: {name} is your team's email client. The bundle it belongs to (Microsoft 365, Google Workspace) stays a vendor; the in-scope pieces (SSO, device management, storage holding customer data) are separate systems.

cloud_platform_production.question: Does customer data live on this provider's infrastructure?
cloud_platform_production.no_implies: Re-classify — may be a regular vendor.

cloud_platform_production.question: If this provider had a multi-hour outage, would your service go down?
Do you have their current SOC 2 report (Type 2 if available)?
cloud_platform_production.yes_implies: Soft prompt: ask the client to upload it under 05-subservice-evidence/.
cloud_platform_production.no_implies: Noted as a finding (CUEC gap). Not blocking.

cloud_platform_production.question: Carve out (rely on their SOC 2) or inclusive (audit them yourself)?
cloud_platform_production.yes_implies: Default: carve out. Inclusive is rare.

managed_database.question: Does customer data live in this database service?
If the database service had an outage, would customers be impacted?
Do you have the vendor's SOC 2 report on file?
Are you using their managed encryption keys, or customer-managed keys?
managed_database.yes_implies: Document the key arrangement; affects what we test on your side.

ai_inference.question: Do your prompts to this provider include customer data?
ai_inference.no_implies: Might still be SSO if their outage breaks your product.

ai_inference.question: If their API was unavailable for hours, would your product still meet commitments?
SOC 2 / ISO / equivalent attestation on file?
Do you have a Data Processing Agreement (DPA) with them?
ai_inference.no_implies: Recommend executing one before report issuance.

payment_processor.question: Do you ever store card numbers, CVV, or full PAN anywhere on your side?
payment_processor.yes_implies: PCI scope expands significantly — flag for separate scoping.

payment_processor.question: If their service was down, would you be unable to fulfill commitments?
SOC 2 + PCI-DSS AOC on file?
payment_processor.yes_implies: Soft prompt: ask for upload of both.

payment_processor.question: Carve out, treat as subservice org?

email_service.question: Do you send transactional or marketing emails containing customer data via this provider?
Would prolonged outage affect your customer commitments?

analytics.question: Does customer-identifying data flow to this analytics provider?
Is the analytics provider material to your service delivery?
Are appropriate consent / opt-out controls implemented on your side?
analytics.yes_implies: Document — affects Privacy TSC if in scope.

dns.question: Does this DNS provider route production traffic?
If DNS was down, would your service be unreachable?

vector_database.question: Do the embeddings stored here encode customer data?
If this service was down, would search / RAG / agent functionality break?
Are you using a managed key or customer-managed key?

llm_observability.question: Do the traces ingested by this tool include user prompts or responses that contain customer data?
If this tool was unavailable, would your debugging capability be affected? (Usually no — non-blocking.)
Is the DPA executed with them?

gpu_compute.question: Does customer data flow through inference / training runs on this provider?
If their compute was unavailable for hours, would your service degrade?
Are model weights / customer data persisted on their storage beyond a single run?

cloud_platform_production.evidence_examples: IAM users + roles export, MFA enforcement screenshot, infra-as-code review, audit log retention config, KMS key list, TLS settings, backup + restore test record

managed_database.evidence_examples: DB user list, role grants, TDE on, backups configured, point-in-time-restore evidence, schema migration controls

identity_provider.evidence_examples: User list with status, MFA policy, conditional access rules, admin role assignments, last access review, password policy

code_repository.evidence_examples: Collaborator list, 2FA enforcement on org, branch protection rules on main, required reviewers, status checks, secret scanning enabled, recent PR sample

ci_cd_pipeline.evidence_examples: Workflow file (.yml/.yaml) review, secret list (names not values), deployment approval requirements, recent run history

monitoring_logging.evidence_examples: User list, retention configuration, sample alerts firing, on-call tied in, log shipping enabled

oncall_alerting.evidence_examples: User list, rotation schedule, escalation policy, recent incident triage record

endpoint_mdm.evidence_examples: Enrolled device list, compliance status, FDE enforcement, lock screen policy, automatic updates, install restrictions

endpoint_edr.evidence_examples: Coverage report (devices protected vs total), recent detections, real-time protection status

secrets_manager_workforce.evidence_examples: Vault membership, sharing policies, admin role list, master password / SSO requirement, audit log enabled

secrets_manager_infra.evidence_examples: Access policy review, rotation schedule, audit log export, secret count + types

backup_service.evidence_examples: Backup schedule, last successful run, retention policy, last restore test record, encryption at rest verification

hr_system.evidence_examples: Admin user list, employee list (active/terminated), offboarding workflow evidence, last termination's deprovisioning record

vulnerability_scanner.evidence_examples: Scan coverage (all repos / hosts scanned), recent scan results, remediation tracking, severity SLAs

cdn_waf.evidence_examples: Admin user list, WAF rule export, recent rule changes, traffic logs, TLS configuration

office_productivity.evidence_examples: User list, admin list, MFA enforcement, sharing rules, conditional access

realtime_data_layer.evidence_examples: Access policies, API keys list, recent config changes, TLS endpoint
